why: Flipping x turns the total S into S - 2x, so there are only N + 1 possible sums. One pass computing min(|S|, min over x of |S - 2x|) is the whole solution.
hints: What happens to the total when you multiply a single element x by -1?
It becomes S - 2x. You may also flip nothing, keeping S.
Compute S, then scan all x for the smallest |S - 2x|, starting from |S|. O(N).
pitfalls: 'At most one' flip: keep the no-flip option |S| (example 3).
Flipping a zero changes nothing; flipping a negative number increases the sum.
Do not just flip the largest element; the best x is the one closest to S / 2.
